title: TAME 120
summary: TAME Flight 120 crashed into the side of Cumbal Volcano while approaching Tulcán airport on a non-precision NDB approach. The first officer, who was flying, approached the NDB from the southwest passing west of the beacon, then flew too fast at 230 knots instead of the required 180 knots. This high speed caused the aircraft to overshoot the intended approach course and fly directly into the western side of Cumbal Volcano at 14700 feet in poor visibility.
probable_cause: The pilot flew the NDB approach at excessive speed of 230 knots instead of 180 knots, causing the aircraft to deviate from the correct approach course and impact the mountain. Poor visibility contributed to the crew's failure to detect the deviation.

factors.evidence: the aircraft was flying at 230 kn, rather than the required 180 knots
the pilot began the turn correctly, but was flying too fast; this took the 727 wide of its intended course
Visibility was very poor at the time of the accident; the wreckage was not found until almost a day later
The aircraft crashed into the side of the mountain at 10:23 AM at an elevation of 14700 ft

events.text: Flight made contact with Tulcán control tower at 29 miles from the NDB

Aircraft flying at 230 knots instead of required 180 knots on approach

title: Iran Air Tours 956
summary: Flight 956 departed from Tehran to Khorramabad at 7:30 a.m. The landing was carried out in bad weather conditions. Approximately 15 mi from the airport, at an altitude of 9,100 ft above sea level, the Tu-154 crashed into the Kuh-e Sefid mountain near the village of Sarab-e Dowreh. The copilot warned the captain of aircraft warnings but was ignored because of the captain's over-confidence.
probable_cause: The landing was carried out in bad weather conditions. Based on the CVR, the copilot warned the captain of the aircraft warnings but was ignored because of the captain's over-confidence. The aircraft could not perform the required IFR approach due to the airport not having the Soviet style navigation aides.

title: Air China 129
summary: Boeing 767 crashed into Mount Dotdae near Gimhae Airport during a circling approach to runway 18R. The crew exercised poor crew resource management and lost situational awareness during the approach, flying outside the circling approach area and delaying the base turn. The aircraft was not equipped with terrain warning systems suited for circling approaches, and the crew had never trained for a circling approach to this airport in the airline's simulator. When the first officer advised the captain to execute a missed approach about five seconds before impact, the captain did not respond.
probable_cause: The crew exercised poor crew resource management and lost situational awareness during the circling approach, flying outside the circling approach area and delaying the base turn. The crew did not execute a missed approach when visual contact with the runway was lost. Contributing factors included lack of training for this specific circling approach, disabled ATC ground surveillance systems, and inadequate awareness of weather minimums for the aircraft type.

title: China Northern Airlines 6136
summary: The McDonnell Douglas MD-80 crashed into the bay near Dalian shortly after the pilot reported fire on board. A passenger named Zhang Pilin apparently set fire to the passenger cabin with gasoline, causing a loss of control and crash. Zhang had purchased seven air insurance policies worth a total of 1,400,000 renminbi before boarding the flight. The investigation showed gasoline was found near Zhang's seat and most passengers died of carbon monoxide inhalation.
probable_cause: A passenger named Zhang Pilin apparently set fire to the passenger cabin with gasoline. Zhang had purchased seven air insurance policies before boarding. The investigation showed gasoline was found near Zhang's seat, and most passengers died of carbon monoxide inhalation. The aircraft crashed in the water at a 90 degree bank angle and 30 degree nose down pitch.

title: China Airlines 611

location.name: Taiwan Strait, 26 miles northeast of Penghu Islands

summary: China Airlines Flight 611 disintegrated in mid-air during climb on May 25, 2002, 20 minutes after takeoff from Taiwan. The in-flight breakup was caused by structural failure from metal fatigue cracks in the vertical stabilizer spar that had originated from an improper repair following a tail strike 22 years earlier at Kai Tak Airport in 1980. The aircraft had accumulated over 64,800 flight hours, and fatigue from repeated pressurization cycles caused tiny cracks to propagate until catastrophic failure occurred.
probable_cause: Metal fatigue cracking from an unapproved repair procedure performed after a tail strike in 1980, where a doubler plate was installed over damaged skin contrary to Boeing structural repair manual requirements, leading to structural failure during climb.

factors.evidence: The aircraft broke into four pieces whilst at FL 350 during climb, with radar data supporting the in-flight breakup theory.
Metal fatigue cracks from a tail strike at Kai Tak Airport on 7 February 1980 propagated over 22 years from repeated pressurization cycles.

The permanent repair of the tail strike was not carried out in accordance with Boeing Structural Repair Manual; China Airlines team installed a doubler over the damaged skin rather than replacing the entire affected skin.
A doubler plate was used to repair damage that was far beyond the scope of what a doubler plate is designed to fix.
Hidden cracks beneath the doubler plate were not detected during maintenance inspections over 22 years of service.

events.text: On 7 February 1980, part of the aircraft's tail scraped along runway at Hong Kong during landing as China Airlines Flight 009.
Aircraft was depressurized and ferried back to Taiwan on same day; temporary repair done the day after; permanent repair conducted from 23 to 26 May 1980.
Flight took off at 15:08 Taipei local time from Taoyuan International Airport.
Aircraft was cleared to climb to flight level 350 (approximately 35,000 feet).
Contact with aircraft was lost; radar data indicate aircraft broke into four pieces at FL 350 during climb to cruise altitude.

title: Überlingen mid-air collision

agencies.name: German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation

summary: On 1 July 2002, a Tupolev Tu-154 and Boeing 757 collided near Überlingen, Germany. A single ATC controller handling two workstations assigned both aircraft to the same altitude. When TCAS issued conflicting instructions, the Tu-154 crew followed the controller's descent instruction instead of their TCAS climb directive, while the 757 crew followed TCAS. Both aircraft ended up descending on a collision course.
probable_cause: The accident was caused by shortcomings in Swiss air traffic control, particularly the single controller managing dual workstations, combined with ambiguities in TCAS procedures. The crew of Flight 2937 disregarded their TCAS guidance in favor of the controller's conflicting instruction.
